[LTIM.2.8.5] **Both clocks are recorded.** A sample in which either clock's
value differs from the previous sample is an observed clock value, and the
engine **must** record it on its event trace, both values together
([RFCS.10.3]). The first sample is an observed clock value. The engine
**must** record a sample before it records the input or the pump boundary the
sample was taken for. A replay restores both clocks from the recording ([RFCS.10.5]),
so `now()`, `monotonic_ns()` and every relative-time mechanism read on replay
exactly what they read when the trace was recorded ([LDET.1.1]).

A recording is complete only if the integrator attaches the stream callback
before the engine's first input or sample. One attached later begins part-way
through the run: its first event's `seq` is not `0` ([LFST.5.3]), and a replayer
**must** refuse it with `DS_ERR_FS_RECORDING_INCOMPLETE`, because the inputs
before it are not in it.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_run_from
idris.note: A step whose sample equals the previous one wrote no `ClockAdvance`, and the replay still runs it under that sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_run_holds_what_was_held
idris.note: 'Every relative-time mechanism read on replay exactly what they read when the trace was recorded', for whatever an engine does with its samples: the replay's final state is the recording's.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__replay_drives_the_engine
idris.note: The clause's replay guarantee at the composed pump, for a tick history.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__first_sample_must_be_recorded
idris.note: THE FIRST SAMPLE MUST BE RECORDED. A recorder that compares the first sample with an assumed starting value (0, 0) and writes nothing when they agree leaves, on a platform whose clocks start there, a trace with no `ClockAdvance`; a replay engine whose clocks start at (7, 7) then holds (7, 7) where the recording held (0, 0). 'The first sample is an observed clock value', by the engine that takes the other answer.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__one_clock_is_not_enough
idris.note: ONE CLOCK ON THE ATOM IS NOT ENOUGH: with the monotonic value restored and the wall value not, a replay reads a `now()` the recording never read. 'Both values together', by the atom that carries one.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__record
idris.note: THE RECORDING of a run: each step's atoms in order, the last recorded sample carried along.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_from
idris.note: The replay of a run from its second step on, the replay's clocks being the sample of the step before: it holds the recording's samples.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_holds_what_was_held
idris.note: 'A replay restores both clocks from the recording, so `now()`, `monotonic_ns()` and every relative-time mechanism read on replay exactly what they read when the trace was recorded': for every clock source, every run and every starting value of the replay's clocks, the samples held on replay are the samples held when recording, step for step.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__replay_mono_only
idris.note: A replay of atoms that carry the monotonic clock alone: a `ClockAdvance` sets the monotonic clock and leaves the wall clock where it was. The refused shape.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__step_atoms
idris.note: The atoms of one step in the clause's engine: the sample's `ClockAdvance` if the sample differs from the one before, THEN the input. Before the first step there is no sample to differ from and the first sample is recorded.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__step_replayed
idris.note: One step replayed when the replay's clocks are the sample of the step before: whether or not the step wrote a `ClockAdvance`, the replay holds the step's sample and goes on with it.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__wall_goes_back_on_replay
idris.note: AND WITH BOTH, A WALL CLOCK THAT GOES BACK IS REPLAYED AS IT WENT: the replay holds (1, 9) and then (2, 4), the later step at the earlier instant. The run in which the clause's 'may move backward' happens, executed.

idris.name: rfcs_10_5__clock_atom_goes_first
idris.note: A recorder that writes the step's input before its `ClockAdvance` makes the replay consume each input under the clocks of the step before: 'both values together' on the trace is not enough, the atom must precede the input it governs.
